newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambia postpones legislative election to Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: Gambia postpones legislative election to Dec 12.

text.p: The West African state of Gambia has pushed back its forthcoming parliamentary election by a day to December 12.
A government statement issued on Tuesday announced the change. The reason for the shift was not immediately clear.
Coupmaker Yahya Jammeh was sworn in as president on October 18 after a September presidential election, designed to launch the restoration of civilian rule.
Jammeh, who toppled civilian independence president Sir Dawda Jawara in July 1994 accusing him of corruption, quit the army to stand.
Jammeh's opponents accused him, the army and the administration of not allowing them a fair hearing during the campaign.
